previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, prior DVT/PE, chronic hemoptysis, ventral hernia, and splenectomy was admitted for acute exacerbation of chronic abdominal pain and worsening hemoptysis. Imaging showed no acute abdominal or pulmonary pathology. His abdominal pain was managed with continuation of oxycodone and initiation of amitriptyline for chronic pain. Hemoptysis and hematuria were attributed to chronic cough and anticoagulation with Lovenox, which may be slightly overdosed given his current weight. Due to syringe limitations, Lovenox dose could not be reduced, and he was discharged on prior dose with hematology follow-up. He remained stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and close outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT & PLAN:  ___ year old man with h/o recurrent DVT with 
IVC filter on chronic lovenox, aortic thrombus, substance abuse 
history / concern for narcotic dependence, anxiety, COPD, HTN, 
HLD, presents with CP, hemoptysis, and found to have bilateral 
PE on CT (new R segmental and subsegmental PEs).  No hemodynamic 
instability.
  
# Bilateral pulmonary emboli, recurrent - factor V leiden 
negative, anticardiolipin negative, has IVC filter.  Failed 
warfarin therapy due to failure to achieve therapeutic levels, 
most likely due to patient non-adherence.  Prior to admission, 
patient was anticoagulated on lovenox ___ bid.  Compared with 
written reports of prior images from ___ of this year, pt has 
new right segmental and subsegmental PE and a left segmental & 
subsegmental PE (previously seen on OSH CT).  Hematology was 
consulted, and the current thought is that PE is secondary to 
patient non-adherence to lovenox anticoagulation.  OSH reports 
state that patient has clot on IVC filter.  Left upper extremity 
ultrasound reveals antecubital thrombus.  Bilateral lower 
extremity ultrasound was negative for DVT.  Decreased lovenox 
dose to 100mg BID given patient's recent 25lb weight loss 
(dosing: 1.0mg/kg BID).    

# Pain management - difficult given pt's chronic pain issues, 
known history of substance abuse, and anxiety, we focused on 
non-narcotic pain medication.  Pt subjectively complained of 
chest and abdominal pain and asked for increased doses of 
narcotics, but verified with pharmacy that he was not prescribed 
with chronic narcotics.  Pt did not have tachycardia, elevated 
BP, or splinting with respiration.  Patient refused tyelenol 
because it upsets his stomach.  Avoided NSAIDs given allergy and 
increased risk of GI bleed.  The patient has a significant 
component of anxiety, which is likely negatively affecting his 
pain control.  Pt received oxycontin 5 mg q4h prn pain, offered 
tyelenol ___ mg q6h prn pain. PCP ___ follow up long term pain 
control regimen.

# Hemoptysis - long history, though long presumed to be caused 
by PE, we evaluated for other possible inflammatory/autoimmune 
processes such as Wegener's to ensure that we are not missing 
another possible cause for hemoptysis.  P-ANCA, C-ANCA were 
negative.  Anti-GBM Ab pending

# Anxiety - we discussed non-pharmacologic / coping strategies 
regarding stress, a significant concern for PCP as well, likely 
contributing to difficult pain control.  We continued home 
hydroxyzine during hospitalization.

CHRONIC MEDICAL CONDITIONS
# COPD:  Continued home meds, no wheezes or productive cough
# HTN:  Continued home meds, BP was well controlled
# HLD:  Simvastatin dose decreased to 20 mg, per pharmacy 
recommendation, in combination with amlodipine, there is an 
increased risk of myopathy with simvastatin doses > 20mg
